name: CALVIN: A Benchmark for Language-Conditioned Policy Learning with Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation Tasks
description: CALVIN (Composing Actions from Language and Vision with Unstructured Exploration) is an open-source robotic manipulation benchmark designed to evaluate language-conditioned policy learning over long horizons in multi-environment settings. Developed at the University of Freiburg, CALVIN provides 24 hours of teleoperated unstructured play data (6 hours each in 4 distinct tabletop environments A, B, C, and D) recorded on a simulated Franka Emika Panda manipulator. Each transition includes static and gripper-mounted RGB-D camera streams, proprioceptive arm telemetry, and tactile contact observations paired with offline human crowd-sourced language annotations.

size.notes: The complete ABCD dataset archive (task_ABCD_D.zip) is 656 GB. The ABC subset (task_ABC_D.zip) is 517 GB and D single-environment subset (task_D_D.zip) is 166 GB.

provenance.collection_method: Unstructured teleoperated play data collection using VR controllers driving a simulated Franka Emika Panda arm in PyBullet, coupled with language instruction labeling.
provenance.curation_notes: Provides 4 distinct tabletop environments (A, B, C, D) with varying table colors, textures, and object layouts to evaluate zero-shot multi-environment policy transfer.
data_sources: Original simulation play collection at Autonomous Intelligent Systems Lab, University of Freiburg
